ABS.summary: The absolute value of the numeric argument x.
ABS.details: The result is of type real.

AND.summary: Performs a bit-wise logical AND operation on two 16-bit values.
AND.details: The result is of type integer.

APPEND.summary: Opens an existing file of type SEQ or USR for writing, and positions the write pointer at the end of the file.

ASC.summary: The PETSCII code of the first character of the string argument, as a number.
ASC.details: ASC returns zero for empty strings.

ATN.summary: The arc tangent of the argument.
ATN.details: A multiplication of the result with 180/π converts the value to the unit ”degrees”.

AUTO.summary: Enables or disables automatic line numbering during BASIC program en- RETURN try.

BACKGROUND.summary: Sets the background colour of the screen.

BACKUP.syntax:
BACKUP U source TO U target
BACKUP D source TO D target [,U unit]
BACKUP.details: The target disk will be formatted and an identical copy of the source disk will be written.

BANK.summary: Selects the memory configuration for BASIC commands that use 16-bit addresses.
BANK.details: A value > 127 selects memory mapped I/O.

BEGIN.summary: The beginning of a compound statement to be executed after THEN or ELSE.
BEGIN.details: Do not jump with GOTO or GOSUB into a compound statement, as it may lead to unexpected results.

BEND.summary: The end of a compound statement to be executed after THEN or ELSE.
BEND.details: The example below shows a quirk in the implementation of the compound statement.

BLOAD.syntax: BLOAD filename [,B bank] [,P address] [,R] [,D drive] [,U unit]
BLOAD.summary: Loads a file of type PRG into RAM at address ,P.

BOOT.syntax:
BOOT filename [,B bank][,P address] [,D drive] [,U unit]
BOOT SYS
BOOT
BOOT.summary: Loads and runs a program or boot sector from a disk.

BORDER.summary: Sets the border colour of the screen.

BOX.syntax:
BOX x0,y0, x2,y2 [, solid]
BOX x0,y0, x1,y1, x2,y2, x3,y3 [, solid]
BOX.details: BOX can be used with four coordinate pairs to draw any shape that can be defined with four points, not only rectangles.

BSAVE.syntax: BSAVE filename, P start TO P end [,B bank] [,R] [,D drive] [,U unit]
BSAVE.summary: Saves a memory range to a file of type PRG.
BSAVE.details: The length of the file is end - start + 2.

BUMP.summary: A bitfield of sprites currently colliding with other sprites or screen data.
BUMP.details: It’s possible to detect multiple collisions, but you will need to evaluate the sprite coordinates to detect which sprites have collided.

BVERIFY.syntax: BVERIFY filename [,P address] [,B bank] [,D drive] [,U unit]
BVERIFY.summary: Compares a memory range to a file of type PRG.
BVERIFY.details: BVERIFY can only test for equality.

C@&.summary: Reads or sets the colour code of a character at given screen coordinates.
C@&.details: C@& is a reserved system variable.

CATALOG.summary: Prints a file catalog/directory of the specified disk.
CATALOG.details: CATALOG is a synonym of DIRECTORY and DIR, and produces the same listing.

CHANGE.syntax:
CHANGE /findstring/ TO /replacestring/ [, line range]
CHANGE ”findstring” TO ”replacestring” [, line range]
CHANGE.summary: Edits the BASIC program currently in memory to replace all instances of one string with another.
CHANGE.details: Almost any character that is not part of the string, including letters and punctuation, can be used instead of /.

CHAR.syntax:
CHAR column, row, height, width, direction, string [, address of character
set]
CHAR.summary: Bitmap graphics: displays text on a graphic screen.
CHAR.details: Notice the start position of the string has different units in the horizontal and vertical directions.

CHARDEF.summary: Changes the appearance of a character.
CHARDEF.details: The character bitmap changes are applied to the VIC character set buffer, which resides in RAM at the address FF7.E000.

CHR$.summary: A string containing one character of the given PETSCII value.
CHR$.details: The argument range is from 0 – 255, so this function may also be used to insert control codes into strings.

CIRCLE.syntax: CIRCLE xc, yc, radius [, flags, start, stop]
CIRCLE.details: CIRCLE is used to draw circles on screens with an aspect ratio of 1:1 (for example: 320 x 200 or 640 x 400).

CLOSE.summary: Closes an input or output channel.
CLOSE.details: Closing files that have previously been opened before a program has completed is very important, especially for output files.

CLR.details: CLR should not be used inside loops or subroutines, as it destroys the return address.

CLRBIT.summary: Clears (resets) a single bit at the address.
CLRBIT.details: CLRBIT is a short version of using a bitwise AND to clear a bit, but you can only clear one bit at a time.

CMD.summary: Redirects the standard output from screen to a channel.
CMD.details: The CMD mode is stopped with PRINT#, or by closing the channel with CLOSE.

COLLECT.summary: Rebuilds the Block Availability Map (BAM) of a disk, deleting splat files (files which have been opened, but not properly closed) and marking unused blocks as free.
COLLECT.details: While this command is useful for cleaning a disk from splat files, it is dangerous for disks with boot blocks or random access files.

COLLISION.summary: Enables or disables a user-programmed interrupt handler for sprite collision.
COLLISION.details: It is possible to enable the interrupt handler for all types, but only one can execute at any time.

COLOR.summary: Sets the foreground text colour for subsequent PRINT commands.
COLOR.details: This is another name for FOREGROUND.

CONCAT.syntax: CONCAT appendfile [,D drive] TO targetfile [,D drive] [,U unit]
CONCAT.summary: Appends (concatenates) the contents of the appendfile to the targetfile.
CONCAT.details: CONCAT is executed in the DOS of the disk drive.

CONT.summary: Resumes program execution after a break or stop caused by an END or RUN STOP statement, or by pressing STOP .
CONT.details: CONT cannot be used if a program has stopped because of an error.

COPY.syntax: COPY source [,D drive] [,U unit] TO [target] [,D drive] [,U unit]
COPY.summary: Copies a file to another file, or one or more files from one disk to another.
COPY.details: The file types PRG, SEQ and USR can be copied.

CURSOR.syntax:
CURSOR <ON | OFF> [{, column, row, style}]
CURSOR column, row
CURSOR.summary: Moves the text cursor to the specified position on the current text screen.
CURSOR.details: When the cursor in ”on,” moving the cursor with PRINT may cause display artifacts where the cursor-on character remains when a PETSCII code relocates the cursor.

CUT.summary: Bitmap graphics: copies the content of the specified rectangle with upper left position x, y and the width and height to a buffer, and fills the region afterwards with the colour of the currently selected pen.
CUT.details: The size of the rectangle is limited by the 1KB size of the buffer.

DATA.summary: Defines constants which can be read by READ statements in a program.
DATA.details: It is good programming practice to put large amounts of DATA statements at the end of the program, so they don’t slow down the search for line numbers after GOTO, and other statements with line number targets.

DCLEAR.summary: Sends an initialise command to the specified unit and drive.

DCLOSE.summary: Closes a single file or all files for the specified unit.
DCLOSE.details: It is important to close all open files before a program ends.

DEC.summary: The decimal value of a hexadecimal string.
DEC.details: Allowed digits in uppercase/graphics mode are 0 – 9 and A – F (0123456789ABCDEF) and in lowercase/uppercase mode are 0 – 9 and a – f (0123456789abcdef).

DECBIN.summary: The decimal value of a binary string.
DECBIN.details: DECBIN ignores everything after the first non-binary digit or the 32nd character.

DEF FN.summary: Defines a single statement user function with one argument of type real, that returns a real value when evaluated.
DEF FN.details: The function argument is not a real variable and will not overwrite a variable with that name.

DELETE.syntax:
DELETE [line range]
DELETE filename [,D drive] [,U unit] [,R]
DELETE.summary: The first form deletes a range of lines from the BASIC program.
DELETE.details: DELETE is a synonym of SCRATCH and ERASE.

DIM.summary: Declares the shape, bounds and the type of a BASIC array.
DIM.details: Byte arrays consume one byte per element, integer arrays two bytes, real arrays five bytes and string arrays three bytes for the string descriptor plus the length of the string itself.

DIR.syntax:
DIR [filepattern] [,W] [,P] [,R] [,D drive] [,U unit]
DIRECTORY [filepattern] [,W] [,P] [,R] [,D drive] [,U unit]
$ [filepattern] [,W] [,R] [,D drive] [,U unit]
DIR [filepattern] ,U12 [,P]
DIR.summary: Prints a file directory/catalog of the specified disk.

DISK.summary: Sends a command string to the specified disk unit.
DISK.details: The command string is interpreted by the disk unit and must be compatible to the used DOS version.

DLOAD.syntax:
DLOAD filename [,D drive] [,U unit]
DLOAD ”$[pattern=type]” [,D drive] [,U unit]
DLOAD ”$$[pattern=type]” [,D drive] [,U unit]
DLOAD.summary: The first form loads a file of type PRG into memory reserved for BASIC programs.
DLOAD.details: The load address that is stored in the first two bytes of the PRG file is ignored.

DMA.syntax:
DMA command [, length, source address, source bank, target address,
target bank[, sub]]
DMA.summary: DMA (”Direct Memory Access”) is obsolete, and has been replaced by EDMA.
DMA.details: DMA has access to the lower 1MB address range organised in 16 banks of 64KB.

DMODE.syntax: DMODE jam, complement, stencil, style, thick
DMODE.summary: Bitmap graphics: sets “display mode” parameters of the graphics context, used by drawing commands.
DMODE.details: The stencil and thick parameters are not implemented and have no effect.

DO.syntax:
DO ... LOOP
DO [<UNTIL | WHILE> logical expression] ... statements [EXIT]
LOOP [<UNTIL | WHILE> logical expression]
DO.summary: DO define the start of a BASIC loop.

DOPEN.summary: Opens a file for reading or writing.
DOPEN.details: DOPEN# may be used to open all file types.

DOT.summary: Bitmap graphics: draws a pixel at screen coordinates (x, y).

DPAT.summary: Bitmap graphics: sets the drawing pattern of the graphics context for drawing commands.
DPAT.details: To use the draw pattern, use DMODE to set the style mode to 1.

DS.summary: The status of the last disk operation.
DS.details: DS is a reserved system variable.

DS$.summary: The status of the last disk operation in text form of the format "<code>,<message>,<track>,<sector>”.
DS$.details: DS$ is a reserved system variable.

DSAVE.summary: Saves the BASIC program in memory to a file of type PRG.
DSAVE.details: DVERIFY can be used after DSAVE to check if the saved program on disk is identical to the program in memory.

DT$.summary: The current date, as a string.
DT$.details: DT$ is a reserved system variable.

DVERIFY.summary: Verifies that the BASIC program in memory is equivalent to a file of type PRG.
DVERIFY.details: DVERIFY can only test for equality.

EDIT.summary: Enables or disables the text editing mode of the screen editor.

EDMA.summary: Copies or updates a large amount of memory quickly.
EDMA.details: EDMA can access the entire 256MB address range, using up to 28 bits for the addresses of the source and target.

EL.summary: The line number where the most recent BASIC error occurred, or the value -1 if there was no error.
EL.details: EL is a reserved system variable.

ELLIPSE.syntax: ELLIPSE xc, yc, xr, yr[, flags , start, stop]
ELLIPSE.details: ELLIPSE is used to draw ellipses on screens at various resolutions.

ELSE.syntax: IF expression THEN true clause [ELSE false clause]
ELSE.summary: ELSE is an optional part of an IF statement.
ELSE.details: There must be a colon before ELSE.

END.summary: Ends the execution of the BASIC program.
END.details: END does not clear channels nor close files.

ENVELOPE.syntax: ENVELOPE n [{, attack, decay, sustain, release, waveform, pw}]
ENVELOPE.summary: Sets the parameters for the synthesis of a musical instrument for use with PLAY.

ER.summary: The number of the most recent BASIC error that has occurred, or -1 if there was no error.
ER.details: ER is a reserved system variable.

ERASE.details: ERASE is a synonym of SCRATCH and DELETE.

ERR$.summary: The string description of a given BASIC error number.
ERR$.details: A BASIC error number out of range (1 – 44) will produce an OK.

EXIT.details: In nested loops, EXIT exits only the current loop, and continues execution in the outer loop (if there is one).

EXP.summary: The value of the mathematical constant Euler’s number (2.71828183) raised to the power of the argument.
EXP.details: An argument greater than 88 produces an Overflow error.

FAST.summary: Sets CPU clock speed to 1 MHz, 3.5 MHz or 40 MHz.
FAST.details: Although it’s possible to call FAST with any real number, the precision part (the decimal point and any digits after it), will be ignored.

FGOSUB.summary: Evaluates the given numeric expression, then call GOSUBs the subroutine at the resulting line number.
FGOSUB.details: Take care when using RENUMBER to change the line numbers of your program that any FGOSUB statements still use the intended numbers.

FGOTO.summary: Evaluates the given numeric expression, then GOTOs to the resulting line number.
FGOTO.details: Take care when using RENUMBER to change the line numbers of your program that any FGOTO statements still use the intended numbers.

FILTER.syntax: FILTER sid [{, freq, lp, bp, hp, res}]
FILTER.summary: Sets the parameters for a SID sound filter.
FILTER.details: Missing parameters keep their current value.

FIND.syntax:
FIND /string/ [, line range]
FIND ”string” [, line range]
FIND.summary: Searches the BASIC program that is currently in memory for all instances of a string.
FIND.details: Almost any character that is not part of the string, including letters and punctuation, can be used instead of the ’/’ (slash).

FN.summary: FN functions are user-defined functions, that accept a numeric expression as an argument and return a real value.

FONT.summary: Updates all characters to the given built-in font.
FONT.details: The additional ASCII characters provided by FONT A and B are only available while using the lowercase character set.

FOR.syntax: FOR index = start TO end [STEP step] ... NEXT [index]
FOR.summary: FOR statements start a BASIC loop with an index variable.
FOR.details: For positive increments end must be greater than or equal to start, whereas for negative increments end must be less than or equal to start.

FOREGROUND.summary: Sets the foreground text colour for subsequent PRINT commands.
FOREGROUND.details: This is another name for COLOR.

FORMAT.details: FORMAT is another name for the HEADER command.

FRE.summary: Statistics about how memory is used, or other system properties.

FREAD#.summary: Reads size bytes from channel to memory starting at the 32-bit address pointer.
FREAD#.details: Keep in mind that the POINTER function with a string argument does not return the string address, but the string descriptor.

FREEZER.details: Entering the FREEZER command is an alternative to holding and releasing RESTORE the key.

FWRITE#.summary: Writes size bytes to channel from memory starting at the 32-bit address pointer.
FWRITE#.details: Keep in mind that the POINTER function with a string argument does not return the string address, but the string descriptor.

GCOPY.summary: Bitmap graphics: copies the content of the specified rectangle with upper left position x, y and the width and height to a buffer.
GCOPY.details: The size of the rectangle is limited by the 1KB size of the buffer.

GET.summary: Gets the next character, or byte value of the next character, from the keyboard queue.
GET.details: GETKEY is similar, but waits until a key has been pressed.

GET#.summary: Reads a single byte from the channel argument and assigns single character strings to string variables, or an 8-bit binary value to numeric variables.
GET#.details: All values from 0 to 255 are valid, so GET# can also be used to read binary data.

GETKEY.summary: Gets the next character, or byte value of the next character, from the keyboard queue.

GO64.summary: Switches the MEGA65 to C64-compatible mode.
GO64.details: If you switch back to the MEGA65 using the SYS 58552, the switch will be immediate.

GOSUB.summary: GOSUB (GOto SUBroutine) continues program execution at the given BASIC line number, saving the current BASIC program counter and line number on the run-time stack.
GOSUB.details: Unlike other programming languages, BASIC does not support arguments or local variables for subroutines.

GOTO.summary: Continues program execution at the given BASIC line number.
GOTO.details: If the target line number is higher than the current line number, the search starts from the current line, proceeding to higher line numbers.

GRAPHIC.summary: Bitmap graphics: initialises the BASIC bitmap graphics system.

HASBIT.summary: True (-1) if the value stored in the address has the given bit set, otherwise false (0).

HEADER.details: HEADER is another name for the FORMAT command.

HELP.summary: Displays information about where an error occurred in a BASIC program.

HEX$.summary: A four or eight character hexadecimal representation of the argument.
HEX$.details: If real numbers are used as arguments, the fractional part will be ignored.

HIGHLIGHT.summary: Sets the colours used for code highlighting.
HIGHLIGHT.details: The system messages colour is used when displaying error messages, and in the output of CHANGE, FIND, and HELP.

IF.syntax: IF expression THEN true clause [ELSE false clause]

IMPORT.summary: Loads BASIC code in text format from a file of type SEQ into memory reserved for BASIC programs.
IMPORT.details: The program is loaded into BASIC memory and converted from text to the tokenised form of PRG files.

INFO.summary: Displays information about the runtime environment.
INFO.details: The INFO command displays information about the BASIC runtime environment, including: • The video mode (PAL, NTSC).

INPUT.summary: Prompts the user for keyboard input, printing an optional prompt string and question mark to the screen.
INPUT.details: The user must take care to enter the correct type of input, so it matches the variable list types.

INPUT#.summary: Reads a record from an input device, e.g.
INPUT#.details: The type and number of data in a record must match the variable list.

INSTR.summary: Locates the position of the string expression needle in the string expression haystack, and returns the index of the first occurrence, or zero if there is no match.
INSTR.details: If either string is empty or there is no match the function returns zero.

INT.summary: The integer part of a number.
INT.details: It is not necessary to use the INT function for assigning real values to integer or byte variables, as this conversion will be done implicitly.

JOY.summary: The state of the joystick for the selected controller port (1 or 2).
JOY.details: The return value of port 3, for two joysticks connected and moved simultaneously, is undefined.

KEY.syntax:
KEY
KEY <ON | OFF>
KEY <LOAD | SAVE> filename
KEY number, string
KEY RESTORE
KEY.summary: Manages the function key macros in the BASIC editor.
KEY.details: The sum of the lengths of all assigned strings must not exceed 240 characters.

LEFT$.summary: A string containing the first n characters from the argument string.
LEFT$.details: Empty strings and zero length are legal values.

LEN.details: BASIC strings can contain any character, including the null character.

LET.summary: Assigns values (or results of expressions) to variables.
LET.details: The LET statement is obsolete and not required.

LINE.summary: Bitmap graphics: draws a line or series of lines.

LINE INPUT.syntax: LINE INPUT [prompt <, | ;>] string variable [, string variable ...]
LINE INPUT.summary: Prompts the user for keyboard input, printing an optional prompt string and question mark to the screen.
LINE INPUT.details: This differs from INPUT in how the input is parsed.

LINE INPUT#.summary: Reads one record per variable from an input device (such as a disk drive), and assigns the read data to the variable.
LINE INPUT#.details: Only string variables or string array elements can be used in the variable list.

LIST.summary: Lists a range of lines from the BASIC program in memory.
LIST.details: The optional parameter P enables page mode.

LOAD.syntax:
LOAD filename [, unit [, flag]]
LOAD ”$[pattern=type]” [, unit]
LOAD ”$$[pattern=type]” [, unit]
/ filename [, unit [, flag]]
LOAD.summary: The first form loads a file of type PRG into memory reserved for BASIC programs.
LOAD.details: LOAD loads files of type PRG into RAM bank 0, which is also used for BASIC program source.

LOADIFF.summary: Bitmap graphics: loads an IFF file into graphics memory.
LOADIFF.details: Tools are available to convert popular image formats to IFF.

LOCK.summary: Locks a file on disk, preventing it from being updated or deleted.
LOCK.details: In direct mode, the number of locked files is printed.

LOG.summary: The natural logarithm of a number.
LOG.details: For convenience, BASIC 65 includes separate functions for logarithms in base 10 and base 2: LOG10() and LOG2(), respectively.

LOG10.summary: The decimal logarithm of the numeric expression.

LOG2.summary: The binary logarithm of the numeric expression.

LOOP.syntax:
DO ... LOOP
DO [<UNTIL | WHILE> logical expression] ... statements [EXIT]
LOOP [<UNTIL | WHILE> logical expression]

LPEN.summary: The state of a light pen peripheral.
LPEN.details: The X resolution is two pixels, therefore LPEN(0) only returns even numbers.

MEM.summary: Reserves memory in banks 4 or 5, such that the bitmap graphics system will not use it.

MERGE.summary: Loads a BASIC program file from disk and appends it to the program in memory.
MERGE.details: The load address stored in the first two bytes of the file is ignored.

MID$.syntax:
MID$(string, index, n)
MID$(string variable, index, n) = string expression
MID$.summary: As a function, the substring of a string.
MID$.details: Empty strings and zero lengths are legal values.

MKDIR.summary: Makes (creates) a subdirectory on a floppy or D81 disk image.

MOD.summary: The remainder of a division operation.
MOD.details: In other programming languages such as C, this function is implemented as an operator (%).

MONITOR.summary: Invokes the KERNAL machine language monitor.
MONITOR.details: Using the MONITOR requires knowledge of the CSG4510 / 6502 / 6510 CPUs, the assembly language they use, and their architectures.

MOUNT.syntax:
MOUNT filename [,U unit]
MOUNT [U unit]
MOUNT OFF [U unit]
MOUNT.summary: Mounts a disk image file of type D81 or D64 from SD card to unit 8 (default) or unit 9 (U9).
MOUNT.details: MOUNT can be used either in direct mode or in a program.

MOUSE.syntax:
MOUSE ON [{, port, sprite, hotspot, pos}]
MOUSE OFF
MOUSE.summary: Enables the mouse driver and connects the mouse at the specified port with the mouse pointer sprite.
MOUSE.details: The ”hot spot” of the mouse specifies where in the mouse sprite image is considered the click target, such as the top of an arrow or the center of a target reticle.

MOVSPR.syntax:
MOVSPR number, position
MOVSPR number, start-position TO end-position, speed
MOVSPR.summary: Moves a sprite to a location on screen.

NEW.summary: Erases the BASIC program in memory, and resets all BASIC parameters to their default values.

NEXT.syntax: FOR index = start TO end [STEP step] ... NEXT [index]
NEXT.summary: Marks the end of the loop associated with the given index variable.
NEXT.details: The index variable after NEXT is optional.

NOT.summary: Performs a bit-wise logical NOT operation on a 16-bit value.
NOT.details: The result is of type integer.

OFF.summary: OFF is a secondary keyword used in combination with primary keywords, such as KEY and MOUSE.
OFF.details: OFF cannot be used on its own.

ON.syntax:
ON expression GOSUB line number [, line number ...]
ON expression GOTO line number [, line number ...]
keyword ON
ON.summary: Performs GOSUB or GOTO to a line number selected by a number expression.
ON.details: Negative values for expression will stop the program with an Illegal Quantity error.

OPEN.syntax: OPEN channel, first address [, secondary address [, filename]]
OPEN.summary: Opens an input/output channel for a device.
OPEN.details: For IEC disk units the usage of DOPEN# is recommended.

OR.summary: Performs a bit-wise logical OR operation on two 16-bit values.
OR.details: The result is of type integer.

PAINT.syntax: PAINT x, y, mode [, region border colour]
PAINT.summary: Bitmap graphics: performs a flood fill of an enclosed graphics area using the current pen colour.

PALETTE.syntax:
PALETTE screen, colour, red, green, blue
PALETTE COLOR colour, red, green, blue
PALETTE RESTORE
PALETTE.summary: PALETTE can be used to change an entry of the system colour palette, or the palette of a screen.

PASTE.summary: Bitmap graphics: pastes the content of the CUT or GCOPY buffer onto the screen.
PASTE.details: The size of the rectangle is limited by the 1KB size of the buffer.

PEEK.summary: The byte value stored in memory at address, as an unsigned 8-bit number.
PEEK.details: Banks 0 – 127 give access to RAM or ROM banks.

PEN.summary: Bitmap graphics: sets the colour (palette entry) of the graphic pen for the current screen.
PEN.details: The C65 design documentation describes a two-argument form of PEN that sets the palette entry for one of two pens: the drawing pen colour (pen 0), and a secondary colour used by the jam drawing mode (pen 1).

PIXEL.summary: Bitmap graphics: the colour of a pixel at the given position.

PLAY.syntax: PLAY [{string1, string2, string3, string4, string5, string6}]
PLAY.summary: Starts playing a sequence of musical notes, or stops a currently playing sequence.
PLAY.details: The PLAY statement makes use of an interrupt driven routine that starts parsing the string and playing the melody.

POINTER.summary: The current address of a variable or an array element as a 32-bit pointer.
POINTER.details: The address values of arrays and their elements are constant while the program is executing.

POKE.summary: Writes one or more bytes into memory or memory mapped I/O, starting at address.
POKE.details: The address is incremented for each data byte, so a memory range can be written to with a single POKE.

POLYGON.syntax: POLYGON x, y, xrad, yrad, sides [{, drawsides, subtend, angle, solid}]
POLYGON.summary: Bitmap graphics: draws a regular n-sided polygon.
POLYGON.details: A regular polygon is both isogonal and isotoxal, meaning all sides and angles are alike.

POS.summary: The cursor column relative to the currently used window.
POS.details: POS gives the column position for the screen cursor.

POT.summary: The position of a paddle peripheral.
POT.details: Analogue paddles are noisy and inexact.

PRINT.summary: Prints a series of values formatted to the current output stream, typically the screen.
PRINT.details: The SPC and TAB functions may be used in the argument list for positioning.

PRINT USING.summary: Prints a series of values formatted using a pattern to the current output stream (typically the screen) or an output channel.

PRINT#.summary: Prints a series of values formatted to the device assigned to channel.
PRINT#.details: The SPC and TAB functions are not suitable for devices other than the screen.

RCOLOR.summary: The current colour index for the selected colour source.

RCURSOR.summary: Reads the current cursor column and row into variables.
RCURSOR.details: The row and column values start at zero, where the left-most column is zero, and the top row is zero.

RDISK.summary: The value of a property of the most recent disk action.

READ.summary: Reads values from DATA statements into variables.
READ.details: It is good programming practice to put large amounts of DATA statements at the end of the program, so they don’t slow down the search for line numbers after GOTO, and other statements with line number targets.

RECORD.summary: Positions the read/write pointer of a relative file.
RECORD.details: The Commodore disk drives have a bug in their DOS, which can destroy data by using relative files.

REM.summary: REM (short for remark) ignores all subsequent characters on a line of BASIC code, as a code comment.

RENAME.syntax: RENAME old TO new [,D drive] [,U unit]
RENAME.details: RENAME is executed in the DOS of the disk drive.

RENUMBER.summary: Renumbers lines of a BASIC program.
RENUMBER.details: RENUMBER may need several minutes to execute for large programs.

RESTORE.summary: Sets the internal pointer for READ from DATA statements.
RESTORE.details: The new pointer target line does not need to contain DATA statements.

RESUME.summary: Resumes normal program execution in a TRAP routine, after handling an error.
RESUME.details: RESUME cannot be used in direct mode.

RETURN.summary: Returns control from a subroutine that was called with GOSUB or an event handler declared with COLLISION.

RGRAPHIC.summary: Bitmap graphics: the status of a given graphic screen parameter.

RIGHT$.summary: A string containing the last n characters from string.
RIGHT$.details: Empty strings and zero lengths are legal values.

RMOUSE.syntax: RMOUSE x variable, y variable, button variable
RMOUSE.summary: Reads mouse position and button status.
RMOUSE.details: RMOUSE places -1 into all variables if the mouse is not connected or disabled.

RND.details: Seeded random number sequences produce the same sequence for identical seeds.

RPALETTE.summary: The red, green, or blue value of a palette colour index.

RPEN.summary: The colour index of pen n.

RPLAY.summary: Tests whether music is playing on the given voice channel.

RPT$.summary: A new string equivalent to string repeated count times.
RPT$.details: If the new string would be longer than 255 characters, this reports a String Too Long error.

RREG.summary: Reads the values that were in the CPU registers after a SYS call, into the specified variables.
RREG.details: The register values after a SYS call are stored in system memory.

RSPCOLOR.summary: The colour setting of a multi-colour sprite colour.
RSPCOLOR.details: Refer to SPRITE and SPRCOLOR for more information.

RSPEED.summary: The current CPU clock in MHz.
RSPEED.details: RSPEED(n) will not return the correct value if POKE 0, 65 has previously been used to enable the highest speed (40 MHz).

RSPPOS.details: Refer to the MOVSPR and SPRITE commands for more information.

RSPRITE.details: Refer to the MOVSPR and SPRITE commands for more information.

RSPRSYS.details: Refer to the SPRITE SYS command for more information.

RUN.syntax:
RUN [line number]
RUN filename [,D drive] [,U unit]
↑ filename
RUN.summary: Runs the BASIC program in memory, or loads and runs a program from disk.
RUN.details: RUN first resets all internal pointers to their default values.

RWINDOW.summary: A parameter of the current text window.
RWINDOW.details: Refer to the WINDOW command for more information.

SAVE.summary: Saves a BASIC program to a file of type PRG.
SAVE.details: SAVE is obsolete, implemented only for backwards compatibility.

SAVEIFF.summary: Bitmap graphics: saves the current graphics screen to a disk file in IFF format.
SAVEIFF.details: Files saved with SAVEIFF can be loaded with LOADIFF.

SCNCLR.summary: Clears a text window or bitmap graphics screen.

SCRATCH.details: SCRATCH is a synonym of ERASE and DELETE.

SCREEN.syntax:
SCREEN [screen,] width, height, depth
SCREEN CLR colour
SCREEN DEF screen, width flag, height flag, depth
SCREEN SET drawscreen, viewscreen
SCREEN OPEN [screen]
SCREEN CLOSE [screen]
SCREEN.summary: Bitmap graphics: manages a graphics screen.
SCREEN.details: Graphics screens are allocated in banks 4 and 5 of memory.

SET.syntax:
SET DEF unit
SET DISK old TO new
SET VERIFY <ON | OFF>
SET.summary: SET DEF redefines the default unit for disk access, which is initialised to 8 by the DOS.
SET.details: These settings are valid until a reset or shutdown.

SETBIT.summary: Sets a single bit at the address.

SGN.summary: The sign of a numeric expression, as a number.

SLEEP.summary: Pauses execution for the given duration.

SOUND.syntax:
SOUND voice, freq, dur [{, dir, min, sweep, wave, pulse}]
SOUND CLR
SOUND.details: SOUND starts playing the sound effect and immediately continues with the execution of the next BASIC statement while the sound effect is played.

SPC.summary: As an argument to PRINT, a string of cursor-right PETSCII codes, suitable for printing to advance the cursor the given number of columns.
SPC.details: The name of this function is derived from “spaces,” which is misleading.

SPEED.summary: Sets the CPU clock speed to 1 MHz, 3.5 MHz, or 40.5 MHz.
SPEED.details: Although it’s possible to call SPEED with any real number, the precision part (the decimal point and any digits after it), will be ignored.

SPRCOLOR.details: The colours used with SPRCOLOR will affect all sprites.

SPRITE.syntax:
SPRITE CLR
SPRITE LOAD filename [,D drive] [,U unit]
SPRITE SAVE filename [,D drive] [,U unit]
SPRITE num [{, switch, colour, prio, expx, expy, mode}]
SPRITE SYS R hires-mode
SPRITE.summary: SPRITE CLR clears all sprite data and sets all pointers and attributes to their default values.

SPRSAV.summary: Copies sprite data between two sprites, or between a sprite and a string variable.
SPRSAV.details: Source and destination can either be a sprite number or a string variable, SPRSAV can be used with the basic form of sprites (C64 compatible) only.

SQR.summary: The square root of a numeric expression.
SQR.details: The argument must not be negative.

ST.summary: The status of the last I/O operation.
ST.details: ST is a reserved system variable.

STEP.syntax: FOR index = start TO end [STEP step] ... NEXT [index]
STEP.summary: STEP is an optional part of a FOR loop.
STEP.details: For positive increments, end must be greater than or equal to start.

STOP.summary: Stops the execution of the BASIC program.
STOP.details: All variable definitions are still valid after STOP.

STR$.summary: A string of the formatted value of the argument, as if it were PRINTed to the string.

STRBIN$.summary: The number value as a string of its binary representation.

SYS.syntax:
SYS address [{, areg, xreg, yreg, zreg, sreg}]
SYS TO address [{,A areg,X xreg,Y yreg,Z zreg,S sreg ,I BASIC interrupt
mode ,O MAPL offset }]
SYS.details: The register values after a SYS call are stored in system memory.

T@&.summary: Reads or sets the screen code of a character at given screen coordinates.
T@&.details: T@& is a reserved system variable.

TAB.details: This function shouldn’t be confused with , which advances the cursor to the next tab-stop.

TEMPO.summary: Sets the playback speed for PLAY.

THEN.syntax: IF expression THEN true clause [ELSE false clause]
THEN.summary: THEN is part of an IF statement.

TI.summary: A high precision timer variable with a resolution of 1 micro second.
TI.details: TI is a reserved system variable.

TI$.summary: The current time of day, as a string.
TI$.details: TI$ is a reserved system variable.

TO.summary: TO is a secondary keyword used in combination with primary keywords, such as BACKUP, BSAVE, CHANGE, CONCAT, COPY, FOR, GO, RE- NAME, and SET DISK.
TO.details: TO cannot be used on its own.

TRAP.summary: Registers (or clears) a BASIC error handler subroutine.

TROFF.summary: Turns off trace mode (switched on by TRON).

TYPE.summary: Prints the contents of a file containing text encoded as PETSCII.
TYPE.details: TYPE cannot be used to print BASIC programs.

UNLOCK.summary: Unlocks a file on disk previously locked using LOCK.
UNLOCK.details: Unlocking a file that is already unlocked has no effect.

UNTIL.syntax:
DO ... LOOP
DO [<UNTIL | WHILE> logical expression] ... statements [EXIT]
LOOP [<UNTIL | WHILE> logical expression]

USING.summary: Parses the format string and evaluates the argument.
USING.details: The format string is only applied for one argument, but it is possible to append more than one USING format;argument sequences.

USR.summary: Invokes an assembly language routine whose memory address is stored at $02F8 – $02F9.
USR.details: Banks 0 – 127 give access to RAM or ROM banks.

VAL.summary: The decimal floating point value represented by a string.
VAL.details: VAL parses characters from the beginning of the string that resemble a BASIC decimal number, including a leading negative sign, digits, a decimal point, and an exponent.

VERIFY.summary: VERIFY with no binflag compares a BASIC program in memory with a disk file of type PRG.
VERIFY.details: VERIFY can only test for equality.

VIEWPORT.syntax:
VIEWPORT CLR
VIEWPORT DEF x, y, width, height
VIEWPORT.summary: Bitmap graphics: manages the viewport of a screen.
VIEWPORT.details: The clipping region can be reset to full screen by the command VIEWPORT DEF 0, 0, WIDTH, HEIGHT using the same values for width and height as in the SCREEN command.

VOL.summary: Sets the volume for sound output with SOUND or PLAY.
VOL.details: The terms ”right” and ”left” refer to the default pan settings for the SID chips in the audio mixer.

VSYNC.summary: Waits until the selected raster line is active.

WAIT.summary: Pauses the BASIC program until a requested bit pattern is read from the given address.
WAIT.details: WAIT is typically used to examine hardware registers or system variables and wait for an event, e.g.

WHILE.syntax:
DO ... LOOP
DO [<UNTIL | WHILE> logical expression] ... statements [EXIT]
LOOP [<UNTIL | WHILE> logical expression]

WINDOW.syntax: WINDOW left, top, right, bottom[, clear]
WINDOW.summary: Sets the text screen window position and size.
WINDOW.details: The row values range from 0 to 24.

WPEEK.summary: The 16-bit word value stored in memory at address (low byte) and address+1 (high byte), as an unsigned 16-bit number.
WPEEK.details: Banks 0 – 127 give access to RAM or ROM banks.

WPOKE.summary: Writes one or more 16-bit words into memory or memory mapped I/O, starting at address.
WPOKE.details: The address is increased by two for each data word, so a memory range can be written to with a single WPOKE.

XOR.summary: Performs a bit-wise logical Exclusive OR operation on two 16-bit values.
XOR.details: The result is of type integer.
